title: Senior Development Finance UK
h1: Not revealed by search results. The indexed page title is "Senior Development Finance UK" (seen identically in results [a] and [b]); the H1 is likely the same or close, but this is not confirmed.
metaDescription: Not revealed. The search tool returned paraphrased summaries, not the meta description.
summary: Product page of the UK broker Silver Oak Capital describing senior development finance: a first-charge loan secured on the development site, presented as the main funding source for large construction projects (from a single bespoke build to a multi-unit housing scheme). It covers a large share of the land purchase and most of the construction costs. The loan is structured in two parts: a day-one tranche to buy the site or refinance an existing bridging loan, and a held-back portion paid out in stages as construction progresses, after certification by a monitoring surveyor. The page positions the firm as focusing on leverage, cash flow and control rather than interest rate alone, and says specialist lenders fill the gap left by high-street banks. No figures (LTV, LTGDV, rates, fees, loan sizes, durations) specific to THIS page were surfaced; the only leverage figure (65-75% of GDV) comes from a separate Silver Oak blog page. Search (c) surfaced nothing about Silver Oak at all.

sections.heading: What senior development finance is (page summary [a][b])
sections.content: Described as the main funding source for large construction projects, from a single bespoke build to a multi-unit housing scheme. It is a first-charge loan / first-charge facility secured on the development site. It covers a large share of the land purchase and most of the construction costs ([a]); [b] phrases it as covering construction and, if needed, the land purchase.

sections.heading: How the loan is structured: two parts (page summary [a][b])
sections.content: A portion is released on day one to buy the site or refinance an existing bridge loan. The rest is held back and paid out in stages as construction progresses, after a monitoring surveyor certifies the work.

sections.heading: Firm's approach (page summary [a])
sections.content: The firm says it focuses on leverage, cash flow, and control rather than the interest rate alone. It also says specialist lenders fill the gap left by high-street banks; the summary attaches 'which assess projects on viability' to this sentence (ambiguous whether it refers to specialist lenders or banks; most plausibly the specialist lenders assess on project viability).

sections.heading: Related leverage figure (NOT from this page) [b][seed]
sections.content: A separate Silver Oak page (the Scotland development finance blog) puts standard senior development loans at roughly 65-75% of Gross Development Value. The stretch senior page says stretch senior can reach up to 75% of GDV or 90% loan-to-cost, usually with tighter covenants.

sections.heading: Related process (NOT from this page) [a][b][seed]
sections.content: The general property development finance page describes an initial consultation, a shortlist of around three or four lenders, then formal heads of terms for the client to review; loans are rolled up and repaid on completion through sales or refinancing.

sections.heading: Related worked example (NOT from this page) [a][seed]
sections.content: The older /types-of-borrowing/ page lists senior, stretched senior, mezzanine and joint venture equity options and gives an indicative example of a GBP 10 million loan at a 6.5% fixed rate over 18 months with a typical broker fee of 1.00%. The search tool flagged that page as about 1,600 days old.

notes: Direct fetch blocked; everything comes from the WebSearch tool's paraphrased summaries of indexed snippets, not from the page HTML. Searches (a) and (b) both surfaced the page and agree on the core mechanism (first charge, two-part drawdown, monitoring surveyor). Search (c) ("Silver Oak Capital" senior development finance "loan to value") returned zero Silver Oak results; everything it returned (Silbury Finance, Oaktree, Live Oak, Hodge Bank, Clifton PF) is unrelated and was ignored. Contradictions/uncertainties: (1) [a] says the loan covers 'a large share of the land purchase', [b] says 'if needed, the land purchase' (land coverage may be optional); (2) the '800+ lenders' figure in [b] is reported as a general Silver Oak claim, unclear whether it appears on this page (seed shows 300+/500+/700+/800+ across pages); (3) the 65-75% GDV leverage is explicitly attributed to a different Silver Oak page, not this one; (4) the sentence about 'which assess projects on viability' has ambiguous attribution. No FAQ, testimonials, awards, meta description, H1 or explicit CTAs for this page were surfaced. Search (a)'s summary also stated it 'searched on the company name rather than the URL' and that page text was 'partly truncated'.
